title: Modeling Retinitis Pigmentosa through Patient-Derived Retinal Organoids
author: Li, Deng, et al.

steps.title: Matrigel coat 6-well plates
steps.instruction: Prepare Matrigel coating solution and apply to plates.

substeps.instruction: Thaw 370 µL Matrigel aliquots at 4 °C for 1–2 days until completely melted.
Add 1 aliquot of Matrigel to 24 mL DMEM/F12 (protein concentration 8.1 mg/mL) at 4 °C using pre‑chilled pipettes; mix well.
Add 1 mL of the Matrigel solution to each well of a 6‑well tissue‑culture plate; incubate 30–60 min at 37 °C before use.

steps.title: Gelatin coat 6-well plates
steps.instruction: Apply gelatin coating to plates for urinary cell culture.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 mL of 0.1 % gelatin to each well of a 6‑well plate.
Gently shake the plate to cover the entire bottom surface.
Incubate 30 min at 37 °C before use.

steps.title: Isolate urinary cells
steps.instruction: Collect, wash, and seed urinary cells onto gelatin‑coated plates.

substeps.instruction: Collect 100–300 mL mid‑stream urine per volunteer; discard the first streams; use sterile disposable bottles and avoid container contact with skin.
Transfer urine into 50‑mL tubes using a 25‑mL pipette immediately.
Centrifuge at 400 × g for 10 min at room temperature (20–25 °C).
Discard supernatant carefully until ≤1 mL liquid remains in the tube.
Resuspend the pellet and collect the liquid from one sample into a 50‑mL tube.
Add 10 mL washing buffer to dilute the sample.
Centrifuge at 200 × g for 10 min at room temperature (20–25 °C).
During centrifugation, aspirate the gelatin solution from the coated plates and wash the plates twice with washing buffer.
Add 1 mL primary medium to each gelatin‑coated well.
After centrifugation, discard supernatant until ≤0.2 mL remains.
Resuspend the sediment in 1 mL primary medium.
Transfer the cells onto the gelatin‑coated 6‑well plates and incubate; perform steps 9–12 in the dark. Ensure plates were freshly gelatin‑coated 0.5–1 h before use.

steps.title: Grid hiPSC colonies
steps.instruction: Cut hiPSC colonies into a checkerboard pattern for picking.

substeps.instruction: Approximately three weeks post‑electroporation, locate well‑separated, hESC‑like hiPSC colonies under an inverted microscope.
Using sharp needles, break each colony into a checkerboard‑shaped grid.
Pick only well‑separated, hESC‑like colonies to ensure clonal origin.

steps.title: Seed colonies onto Matrigel plates
steps.instruction: Pick colony fragments and culture them on fresh Matrigel‑coated wells.

substeps.instruction: Collect colony pieces with 100‑µL pipette tips; replace the needle and tip after each pick.
Transfer each piece to a freshly Matrigel‑coated well containing TeSR‑E8 medium supplemented with 10 µM Y‑27632; seed one colony per well.
Ensure the Matrigel‑coated plates were freshly coated 0.5–1 h before use.
